sophia: FYI PR #498 adds a short 'compat shim' and an Optimize migration blurb. Need a quick docs sanity pass + a compact migration checklist. PR: https://github.com/redwood/optimize/pull/498 :link:
raj: On it. Can someone paste a minimal end-to-end snippet showing batching + kv-prefetch? We should prefer tiny working examples, not long explanations.
anya: Here's a concise Python example that highlights batching and cache prefetching (v2 SDK):
```py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD'))
# batch two prompts, enable kv prefetch to warm cache for chat-like flow
resp = client.batch.text.generate([
  {"model": "redwood/opt-2", "prompt": "Summarize the incident logs"},
  {"model": "redwood/opt-2", "prompt": "Extract error codes"}
], options={"kv_prefetch": True})
for r in resp:
  print(r.text)
```
This keeps the example small and shows options as kwargs.
kevin: For quant profiles I'll propose a compact YAML snippet to include in the docs. Key recommends: q8_0 or q4_0 for most production, but add a fallback for tiny inputs. Example I left in the PR comments: 
```yaml
precision: q8_0
kv_prefetch: true
prefetch_policy: aggressive
shortseq_policy:
  max_tokens: 15
  fallback_precision: float32
```
Note: call out that shortseq_policy is conservative—helps avoid weird probability shifts for very short completions.
sophia: Nice. Also add one-line cost heuristics: "Expect ~2.5-4x memory reduction with q8/q4, but validate on a small held-out set; vary precision for latency vs quality tradeoffs."
raj: I'll add a tiny Node example that demonstrates client.batch() and streaming-friendly options: 
```js
const { Client } = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD })
// batch with kv prefetch
const responses = await client.batch.text.generate([
  { model: 'redwood/opt-2', prompt: 'Summarize the logs' },
  { model: 'redwood/opt-2', prompt: 'List anomalous lines' }
], { kv_prefetch: true, stream: false })
responses.forEach(r => console.log(r.outputText))
```
kevin: Adding to docs: small QA note — if customers see hallucinations after quantizing, try q8_0 first, then fallback to float32 for the problematic prompt set. Also include a pointer to the Eval playbook.
anya: One editorial nit: prefer shorter variable names in snippets so they copy easily. Also include a one-line migration checklist in the PR description: 1) update SDK calls (text.generate -> client.text.generate), 2) add quant profile yaml + shortseq fallback, 3) run small smoke eval (10 prompts) and paste token/cost delta, 4) link to console quant profiles page.
sophia: Good. Can someone run the smoke eval and paste numbers? Even a tiny table is fine.
raj: I'll run 10 prompts (current float32 vs q8_0) and paste numbers to PR by EOD.
